posts.title: Inside BLACKPINK's Solo Wave, Where Each Member Is Heading While the Group Rests
posts.excerpt: All four members released new music of their own within three weeks, while the stadium tour that just ended remains the biggest thing they have done.
posts.body:
The busiest stretch of BLACKPINK's year happened without a group release. Between August 28 and September 17, all four members put out new music under their own names, each through a different door. JENNIE opened the run with her *Fallen Angel* EP. LISA followed with "SaWaDiKa," then a version of the same song credited to both her and JENNIE. JISOO delivered "CLICK," the first taste of her debut full-length album. ROSГ‰ closed the window with "new trick," a single whose video was filmed entirely on an iPhone 18 Pro for Apple's Shot on iPhone campaign.

The pattern only reads as a wave because of what came before it. The Deadline World Tour, the group's first all-stadium run, opened at Goyang Stadium in South Korea in July 2025 and closed at Kai Tak Stadium in Hong Kong on January 26. In February the four released *Deadline*, their first project since *Born Pink* in 2022, a five-track EP led by JUMP and GO. JUMP had been premiered at the tour's opening weekend before it was even a single, and its video has since climbed past 430 million views.

[youtube:CgCVZdcKcqY]

The architecture behind all this was set in advance. At the end of 2024 every member renewed her group contract with YG Entertainment while building separate homes for solo work. Jennie runs Odd Atelier, Lisa has LLOUD, RosГ© signed with Atlantic, Jisoo founded Blissoo. The group became the shared stadium, the solos the main event. On Spotify the four now pull between eight and fifty million monthly listeners apiece, just under 100 million combined, and no single company owns all of it.

JENNIE went first, and she went big. *Fallen Angel* arrived August 28 through Odd Atelier in partnership with Columbia Records, three tracks called FALLEN ANGEL, HEAVEN and Less than a Lover. It is her first collection since *Ruby*, last year's full-length solo debut, which opened at No. 7 on the Billboard 200 and moved more than a million copies worldwide in its first week. Her lane has been consistent since then, rap-forward pop with a taste for the theatrical, and *Fallen Angel* sharpens it. The title-track video plays like a dark fairytale, all fire and feathers, and Billboard readers voted it the best new music of its release week. The lesson of *Ruby* was that she could carry an album on charisma alone. The lesson of the EP is that the charisma has found a setting.

[youtube:s466YCiHfKw]

[photo:https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0e/Jennie_performs_Like_Jennie_at_SoFi_Stadium_01.png/1280px-Jennie_performs_Like_Jennie_at_SoFi_Stadium_01.png|theCwE / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 3.0)|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Jennie_performs_Like_Jennie_at_SoFi_Stadium_01.png|50% 25%|1]

ROSГ‰ closed the window with "new trick," and the song doubles as a technology showcase. Dave Meyers, the director behind some of the most-watched videos of the last decade, shot the whole clip on an iPhone 18 Pro as part of Apple's Shot on iPhone series. The single extends the run she has been on since *rosie*, her 2024 debut album, and since "APT.," her duet with Bruno Mars that turned into the biggest hit any member of the group has touched as a soloist. At the Brit Awards on February 28 she took International Song of the Year for it, the first K-pop artist ever to win at the ceremony. Her lane is the singer-songwriter end of the group, guitars and heartache under the pop polish, and "new trick" stays inside it while playing a new game with the visuals.

[youtube:Lufa9QAFFeY]

[photo:https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/31/Ros%C3%A9_performs_3am_at_SoFi_Stadium_01.png/1280px-Ros%C3%A9_performs_3am_at_SoFi_Stadium_01.png|theCwE / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 3.0)|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ros%C3%A9_performs_3am_at_SoFi_Stadium_01.png|50% 25%|1]

LISA's story right now lives as much on screens as on speakers. She made her acting debut in the third season of The White Lotus, and Netflix has cast her in TYGO, an action thriller set in the Extraction universe alongside Don Lee and Lee Jin-uk, slated for release later this year. In February she was reported as the lead of a romantic comedy inspired by Notting Hill, with producing duties attached. The music keeps pace. "SaWaDiKa" arrived September 1, and a week later a duet version credited LISA and JENNIE together, the first time two members of the group shared a single during this solo wave. Her lane is the most global of the four, dance-pop built for festivals, and the Thai-language title of the single is its own statement about where her audience lives.

[apple:song:6809951680:6809951681]

[photo:https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/LISA_Live_from_The_Deadline_Tour_at_SoFi_Stadium_01.png/1280px-LISA_Live_from_The_Deadline_Tour_at_SoFi_Stadium_01.png|theCwE / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 3.0)|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:LISA_Live_from_The_Deadline_Tour_at_SoFi_Stadium_01.png|50% 25%|1]

JISOO is the patient one, and her rollout says so. After the *AMORTAGE* mini-album in February 2025, she opened September with "CLICK" on the fourth, the first of what she has described as multiple pre-release singles ahead of her debut full-length album. The video drew tens of millions of views in its first two weeks and sat near the top of YouTube's global music chart. Her lane is the warmest of the four, classic pop songwriting with a soft center, closer to a love letter than a mission statement. The acting resume, from the K-drama *Snowdrop* onward, gives her the widest audience overlap outside music, and the singles rollout treats that audience as something to be kept, not spent.

[apple:song:6805983708:6805983713]

[photo:https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/Jisoo_performs_Earthquake_at_SoFi_Stadium_01.png/1280px-Jisoo_performs_Earthquake_at_SoFi_Stadium_01.png|theCwE / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 3.0)|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Jisoo_performs_Earthquake_at_SoFi_Stadium_01.png|50% 25%|1]

The group's own formula explains why the solos work. BLACKPINK records duels, rap verses traded like taunts against choruses built to be screamed by 60,000 people, drops where other bands put bridges. The formula made them the biggest girl group of their era and it also split each song between four voices. The solo wave lets each member keep her half of the duel and live in it. Jennie took the theatre, Lisa the dance floor, RosГ© the guitars, Jisoo the melody. Heard back to back, the four September releases sound like the group's sound separated into its ingredients.

Even the business scaffolding is quietly being rebuilt. *Deadline* was the first group project distributed by The Orchard, the Sony-owned independent distributor, instead of Interscope, the label that carried *Born Pink*. Four women, four companies, one shared stadium circuit. That structure did not exist for K-pop's last generation of supergroups, and the duet between Lisa and Jennie suggests the companies are not rival camps but flexible alliances.

No next group record has been announced. What exists instead is four solo careers running at full speed, each one feeding the name it came from. The fear in 2024 was that contract season would pull BLACKPINK apart. The last three weeks are the argument against that fear, played out in public, one release at a time.

posts.title: UGLY
posts.excerpt: His second album lands January 22 on Warner Records. The first single, "Perfect Man," opens as a piano confession and grows into full-band soul.
posts.body:
Teddy Swims has a second album on the way. *UGLY* arrives January 22 on Warner Records, and the announcement came with its first single, "Perfect Man," a song that opens as a sparse orchestral piano ballad and slowly grows into a warm, full-band soul number carried by an eight-piece string and horn section. Its performance video, filmed live with the full ensemble, is below.

The single is a confession about impossible standards, and it means two things at once. The hook, "There's no such thing as a perfect man," begins as an excuse and ends as a discovery, and by the final verse the song has quietly reversed its own accusation.

"'Perfect Man' is a song about self forgiveness," he said in the release. "In my life, I've held myself to a standard that is completely unrealistic, I've been too hard on myself as a partner, as a father, and in feeling the responsibility that comes with knowing there are people who rely and look up to me. I truly believe our insecurities and our quirks are signs of strength rather than weakness. My hope with this song, and with the work and conversations around it, is that people can find some relief and try to lean into our shortcomings and have an open dialogue about them rather than trying to hide them."And as he put it elsewhere in the announcement, "The beauty of chasing perfection is knowing we will never reach it."

[youtube:yL_KN7kBD7A]

The album was written across the fifteen months since his son was born, and the press materials frame it as an outlet for self-reflection and growth as both a man and a father. Spotify and Apple list thirteen songs on the tracklist, and the credits reunite him with the crew behind his biggest records, Julian Bunetta, Afterhrs, Matt Zara, Mikky Ekko, Kendrick Nicholls and Alex Izquierdo, plus Edgar Barrera.

The arrival comes on the heels of a run that changed the size of his career. "Lose Control," the single that broke him, was certified Diamond by the RIAA in November, the two-hundredth song in U.S. history to reach ten million certified units, and the run also carried his first Grammy nomination and a performance on the Grammy stage. His debut album, *I've Tried Everything but Therapy*, turned all of that momentum into an arena headlining run that has kept him on the road most of the year.

The Ugly Tour opens its arena run on September 22 in Kansas City, with Natasha Bedingfield, Avery Anna and Wyatt Flores among the support acts along the route, and the schedule runs deep into the fall. *UGLY* follows on January 22, once the road goes quiet. Announcing it, he kept the caption as simple as the title, writing only, "This album means a lot."

posts.title: Cardi B Says Her Third Album Is Coming in 2027, and She Isn't Waiting Eight Years This Time
posts.excerpt: Backstage in Las Vegas she laid out the plan, a recording stretch that starts after her birthday in November, with two songs already recorded.
posts.body:
Cardi B has a third album on her calendar. Backstage at the iHeartRadio Music Festival in Las Vegas on Friday, September 18, she told The Breakfast Club that the follow-up to *AM I THE DRAMA?* is already moving, and she plans to release it in 2027.

The plan has a shape. After her birthday in November she steps away from everything else to record. She has two recorded songs she likes and a long way to go, and no patience for the old timeline. When co-host Charlamagne Tha God asked whether she would make fans wait another eight years, her answer was one word. "Nope."

"I am doing a new album. And after November, after my birthday, I'm shifting myself away just to record," she said. "I'm not even playing around," she continued. "I just got this confidence," she added, before singing a line of Patti LaBelle's "New Attitude."

She has not been quiet in between. July brought "AH HA," her first solo single of 2026, a DJ SwanQo production that debuted at No. 25 on the Hot 100 and has since climbed to No. 3 on Billboard's Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart.

At the end of August the song got its visual, and the clip plays like a block party the whole borough shows up to. Directed by Arrad, it turns Brooklyn into her parade ground, neon outfits, dance crews spilling across the sidewalk, a Kash Doll cameo, and it cleared a million views in its first fourteen hours. Watch it below.

[youtube:I-5e_J3LWS8]

Her career has always run on moments exactly like that one. "Bodak Yellow" made her the first woman to take a solo rap single to the top of the Hot 100 in nineteen years, nobody had done it since Lauryn Hill in 1998, and the song later became the first solo rap track by a woman certified Diamond. Nine years and a billion YouTube views later, it is still the reason a third Cardi B album counts as an industry event and not just another release.

The timing is worth taking seriously. *AM I THE DRAMA?* landed in September 2025, her first album since *Invasion of Privacy*, and opened at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 with 200,000 units, making her the first female rapper whose first two albums debuted on top. The Little Miss Drama Tour behind it ran 35 dates from February through April and grossed more than $70 million on 453,000 tickets, according to Billboard Boxscore. The album still carries the hits that built her name, including "WAP," which recently earned Diamond certification for moving ten million units.

There is one more stage before the studio hibernation. On October 18 she headlines BZR WKND at Kingston's National Stadium in Jamaica, her first-ever headlining stadium concert in the Caribbean, a booking Billboard reported back in August. Snoop Dogg and Major Lazer are on the bill. After that, the recording begins in earnest, and this time the wait has a number attached.

posts.title: Taylor Swift's 11 VMA Nominations Put the All-Time Record Within Reach
posts.excerpt: Two more nods arrived with the social categories. The show lands in Los Angeles on September 27, and one win would make the all-time record hers alone.
posts.body:
MTV added the social categories to the 2026 VMAs race on Friday, and the updated board now reads Madonna thirteen, Taylor Swift eleven. The ceremony airs live from Los Angeles on Sunday, September 27, on CBS, and Madonna is booked to open the night with special guests.

The interesting number is not the nominations. Swift is tied with BeyoncГ© at thirty VMA wins, the most the show has ever seen. Madonna, with nineteen career wins, would need almost all of her thirteen nominations to go her way to match them. The show has been handing out moonmen since 1984, and in four decades only two artists have ever reached thirty. That is the company now on the table.

*The Life of a Showgirl* did the heavy lifting on the ballot. "The Fate of Ophelia" carries seven nods by itself, from Video of the Year and Best Pop down through the technical fields, including cinematography, editing, and choreography. Hear the song that anchors the ballot below.

[apple:song:1838810949:1838810951]

 "Opalite" picked up a Best Direction nomination. Artist of the Year is on the list, and the album itself is up for Best Album.

"Opalite" and the album nod mean she can win on the song, the video, and the record in one sitting.

The Song of the Summer slot went to "I Knew It, I Knew You", the track she wrote for the Toy Story 5 soundtrack, and it might be the most surprising line on the whole ballot. A country-tinged ballad written for a Pixar film beat an entire summer of lead singles to take the fan-voted prize. It is her fourteenth country radio No. 1, and she won the same award in 2024 with "Fortnight", so the category clearly agrees with her. The video, a montage cut from scenes across the Toy Story films, gives the song its visual side, and it is below.

[youtube:hDU4GB1PTxc]

The timing makes for a crowded Sunday. Her husband, Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, plays in Miami that afternoon, hours before the show goes live in Los Angeles. If she is on that sideline, she is missing her own history night.

All of it funnels into one number. Thirty wins, tied with BeyoncГ© for the most in VMA history, and eleven nominations mean eleven ways to break the tie. One victory in Los Angeles would put her name alone at the top of the all-time list.

posts.title: Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album Reveals First Six Tracks Ahead of November 19
posts.excerpt: Travis Scott over a Daft Punk beat, Keith Richards at eighty-two, and one track pulling five time zones at once. The wait for Vice City just got louder.
posts.body:
Rockstar Games and Atlantic Records have detailed *Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album*, a set of 34 original tracks built for the game's return to Vice City and the state of Leonida. The record itself is not out yet. It lands November 19, the same day Grand Theft Auto VI launches on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, with the pre-order already up. What dropped today is the first wave, six songs that run from SoundCloud rap to country and Latin club music.

The roster jumps genres on purpose. Yung Lean opens with "That's It" alongside Future and Metro Boomin. Travis Scott brings "RHYNO", produced by Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo, the Daft Punk half who has kept a low profile since the duo's split. Morgan Wallen holds down the country slot with "Last Thing You Need". Rauw Alejandro takes "Macacoa 2000" into Latin territory. Keith Richards closes the first wave with "Bright Lights, Big City", a solo turn from the Rolling Stones guitarist at eighty-two. Guy-Manuel built it like a low rider for a game people have waited thirteen years to play.

The booking matters more than it looks on a tracklist. The Swedish rapper was a SoundCloud outsider a decade ago, and slotting him between Future and Metro Boomin on the first wave is the franchise doing what it has always done, pulling the underground and the mainstream into one playlist.

The six also include "Sexy Magic", a team-up shared by Argentina's CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso, PinkPantheress, Fred again.., and Etienne de CrГ©cy. One song pulling that many time zones together is the album's whole idea in miniature.

[apple:song:6812476690:6812477088]

The Scott single is the one with the loudest credit on the production sheet. Guy-Manuel has produced little outside Daft Punk in recent years, and pairing him with Travis Scott is exactly the kind of swing this series goes for.

The spread is the point. Grand Theft Auto has always been a radio station you can drive through, and the series' soundtracks have doubled as era documents since Vice City put 1980s pop back on repeat. This one works differently. Instead of licensing old hits, Rockstar and Atlantic commissioned a full record of originals, and the album is built to sit alongside the game's radio stations, its dynamic score, and the musical touchpoints of the world. Atlantic, the label behind some of the biggest soundtrack campaigns of the last decade, has assembled a roster that runs from Buenos Aires to Nashville to San Juan.

The commercial stakes are not small. Grand Theft Auto V remains one of the best-selling entertainment products ever made, and the series has near half a billion units sold across its history. A soundtrack attached to that machine arrives with an audience most festival lineups could not assemble in a decade.

The physical run is its own collectible market. Pre-orders opened with a liquid-filled vinyl, a splatter edition, and a jewel-case CD, each with exclusive artwork, plus retailer variants through Blood Records, Best Buy, Walmart, Target, Urban Outfitters, and independent stores.

The series has form here. Vice City turned an out-of-print Eighties canon into a decade-long revival. San Andreas did the same for Nineties hip-hop, and V made a radio dial feel like a festival poster. Atlantic is not scoring a game so much as inheriting the most-watched playlist in entertainment, one that keeps streaming long after the credits.

The story follows Jason and Lucia through a criminal conspiracy across a fictional Florida, and the album's remaining twenty-eight tracks arrive with the game on launch day. The first six are already streaming. November 19 is when the game hits consoles, and the album now has a same-day seat at the table.

posts.title: Bass Persuades
posts.excerpt: The first record without a last name. Electroclash thunder, Pink Floyd drift and a tender sixties-style love song to Maxx Morando.
posts.body:
The tenth MILEY album answers to one word. *Bass Persuades* is out on Atlantic Records, ten tracks in thirty-seven minutes, and the first record released without a Cyrus after the name. The rebrand came first. In August the artist page went from Miley Cyrus to MILEY, the album followed within a day, and the title has carried the argument since. Bass, she has explained, stands for everything that persuades a heart, the fullness and the heartache and the living in between. The sound swings between electroclash and psychedelia, and the record spends its thirty-seven minutes making the same case ten different ways.

The rollout ran on her own clock. She said last year that the next record was already ordered, twelve songs waiting on a private playlist, because long campaigns bore her. Atlantic signed her in the summer, her first label move since Columbia, and the first days of September brought the title track as the lead single. Mert Alas shot the first video, and it set the temperature for everything that came after.

The clip puts the chorus on the street. MILEY works in leather under hard light, surrounded by a dance crowd that looks like it has somewhere better to be, and the tension between their cool and the beat's insistence carries the whole thing. The kids don't wanna dance, she sings, over a track that refuses to take the answer. It is a first impression built the way the album works, a dare wrapped in groove, and it landed the single before anyone had heard the full record.

[youtube:aWpw-Ynl0Yc]

The second clip goes softer without going small. "Let's Get Married" is a love song to her fiancГ© Maxx Morando that could have come off a sixties songbook, elegant chords and no hurry, and the video hangs it around the Chateau Marmont, evening light and a suite that feels like an afterparty nobody is in a hurry to leave. Where the first video dared, this one invites. Together they map the record's two instincts, street-level provocation and late-night devotion, and the album spends its thirty-seven minutes walking between them.

[youtube:qwaVhOZkAek]

The tracklist is wider than the single let on. "Different Religion" opens the door hard, 2002-vintage electroclash with the Brooklyn noise band Model/Actriz chanting along about fast cars and new beginnings. "Orbit" floats on Pink Floyd synths over a country twang, a song about wanting to circle one person forever that quietly reconnects the Dead Petz thread. "Neon Signs" hands the night to Andrew Wyatt of Miike Snow and comes out shaped like a Thompson Twins single. "Innocent Ways" is the quiet center, written around her sister Noah and the kind of family history that sings easier than it speaks. The closing "Bass Persuades Remixx" gives the title back to Model/Actriz and lets the drums finish the record.

[apple:album:6807197456]

Morando sits behind most of it, co-writer and co-producer and now collaborator in the same house, with Kid Harpoon and Michael Pollack carrying over the writing room from the last two records. She has called this the album that means the most to her, and the love story threaded through the tracklist explains part of it. The rest is craft. Ten albums deep, the surprise is still part of the product, and no track overstays its welcome.

The stage plan follows the record instead of leading it. Two Hollywood Bowl nights on October 16 and 18 carry the album title, with Model/Actriz opening, and they stand as MILEY's first full concerts since the stadium era. She calls the venue her favorite place to hear music. That is the entire itinerary so far.

The Bowl nights will pass quickly. *Bass Persuades* is the part that stays, ten songs and a name in capitals, persuading on every track.

posts.title: ROSГ‰ Drops "new trick" With a Dave Meyers Video Shot Entirely on iPhone 18 Pro
posts.excerpt: One phone, one lollipop: ROSГ‰'s "new trick" lands with a Dave Meyers video shot entirely on the iPhone 18 Pro вЂ” and a first taste of the era she promises for next year.
posts.body:
ROSГ‰ is back with a new single: "new trick" arrived on Sept. 17 with a music video shot on nothing but a phone. The Dave Meyers-directed clip was filmed entirely on the iPhone 18 Pro, the newest installment of Apple's "Shot on iPhone" campaign.

The video places ROSГ‰ in the lineage of pop spectacles the series has built its name on: The Weeknd's "Dancing in the Flames," shot on iPhone 16 Pro, Olivia Rodrigo's "get him back!," shot on iPhone 15 Pro Max, and Lady Gaga's "Stupid Love," shot on iPhone 11. Apple and ROSГ‰ announced the partnership on Sept. 9, and the video landed with the single, giving the song a visual debut scaled to her global audience.

The first taste stayed playful. In the teaser, ROSГ‰ holds a purple-burgundy lollipop whose wrapper reads "new trick," while the audio moves from a softer confession вЂ” "Maybe I'm emotional, I lay my dreams out on the table, love is unconditional, it disappears just like a rainbow" вЂ” into a hook built for shouting: "Lovesick, I'll pick my heart off the floor / New trick, watch this, watch this, ow!" A distorted electric guitar and stacked vocals give the snippet a grittier edge than her *rosie* era вЂ” a deliberate feint, exactly as the title promises.

[youtube:Lufa9QAFFeY]

The full track keeps that shape: a softened, multi-tracked verse, then a hook that turns into a chant, with the distorted guitar entering as it turns and stacked vocals piling on top. The reference points sit between eras вЂ” the sheen of a 90s rom-com soundtrack, the punk-rock edge of the early aughts вЂ” while the production stays dry enough to let the guitar noise and the chant carry the hook.

Meyers, whose credits include videos for Taylor Swift, Harry Styles, Kendrick Lamar and Ariana Grande, directed the clip using only the iPhone 18 Pro camera system, which brings variable aperture control to the iPhone for the first time. True to the "Shot on iPhone" framing, every frame comes from the phone; the video keeps ROSГ‰ in bright, playful settings that match the song's uplift.

Handing a director of his stature a phone instead of a cinema camera package is the campaign's quiet argument: the grammar of a big-budget video вЂ” choreography, sets, night exteriors вЂ” can now come out of a pocket-sized sensor. Apple has run the campaign since 2015, when user-shot photos went up on billboards and bus shelters worldwide, with the music-video branch as its newest and loudest form.

In a *VOGUE* interview last week, ROSГ‰ called "new trick" "possibly the cutest thing [she and co-writer Amy Allen] have ever made together," and framed it as a step toward something bigger: she is "still in the process of finding the perfect fine line between the world I want to create, how much of that expresses who I am today, and who I, personally and as a musician, am evolving into," with plans to "introduce a new era of my music next year."

[photo:data:image/jpeg;base64,|Kenneth Cappello|https://www.kennethcappello.com/|51.7% 51.5%|1.06]

For ROSГ‰, "new trick" is the first solo move since *rosie*, her debut studio album, arrived in December 2024, and since "APT.," her duet with Bruno Mars, peaked at No. 3 on the Billboard Hot 100, collected three GRAMMY nominations and ended 2025 as the world's best-selling single. The Korean-New Zealand star has passed 10 billion solo streams вЂ” and that is before counting her tally as a member of BLACKPINK, one of the best-selling girl groups of all time.

The single's visual identity is bound to a device launch: Apple's channels premiered the clip, while ROSГ‰'s own socials carry the behind-the-scenes cuts and the #ShotoniPhone18Pro tag вЂ” a rollout that trades red-carpet spectacle for a making-of feed.

"new trick" is out now on all major streaming platforms, with the video premiering on Apple's channels and on ROSГ‰'s YouTube. On the timeline she sketched last week, it is the opening move of a new era arriving next year.

posts.title: Charli xcx's Music, Fashion, Film Tour Is Under Way, and Europe Is On Sale
posts.excerpt: The North American run opened in Philadelphia last week. UK and Europe tickets for February 2027 went on general sale Friday, with Audrey Hobert opening.
posts.body:
Charli xcx's Music, Fashion, Film Tour is already on the road in North America, and the UK and Europe dates for February 2027 went on general sale Friday. She is not teasing a tour so much as continuing one. Underscores opens the American and Canadian shows. Audrey Hobert opens Europe.

The run started September 11 at Philadelphia's Xfinity Mobile Arena. Two nights at Brooklyn's Barclays Center followed. Toronto's Scotiabank Arena is next, then Boston's TD Garden, Washington's Capital One Arena, Atlanta's State Farm Arena, San Diego's Viejas Arena, two nights at Los Angeles' Kia Forum, Glendale's Desert Diamond Arena, and a close at Las Vegas' MGM Grand Garden Arena on October 23. Austin City Limits sits in the middle of that itinerary, on October 2 and 9. Live Nation has the routing. A limited number of $25 Angel Tickets, with seats assigned at random the day of the show, are part of the North American sale.

*Music, Fashion, Film* arrived July 24, her seventh studio album, and it leans into guitars, with "Rock Music" and "SS26" as the first songs she put in public. The cover, shot by Aidan Zamiri, puts John Cale, Marc Jacobs, and Martin Scorsese in the frame, one figure for each word in the title.

[apple:album:6774745611]

Philadelphia made the live case in a single night. The set opened on "Rock Music," gave "Persona" its first airing of the tour, and closed on "SS26" and "No One Lasts Forever," which is where you put a record you mean to keep. Mid-set she brought Underscores out for "Do It." The rest of the 29 songs kept the catalog in the room, including "Apple," "Von Dutch," "365," "360," "Guess," "party 4 u," and "Vroom Vroom." The new material has to stand next to the songs that already own the floor.

February 2027 adds Dublin's 3Arena on the 13th, then Glasgow's OVO Hydro, Manchester's Co-op Live, London's O2, Amsterdam's Ziggo Dome, and Paris' Accor Arena on the 24th. Artist presale ran September 16. General sale opened Friday at 9 a.m. BST.

Underscores comes from the electronic side of her catalog, and Audrey Hobert opens Europe as a singer, so the same set has to work on both bills. Philadelphia already put the new songs at both ends of the night, next to the *Brat* singles that still fill the room.

posts.title: Drake's FOMO Film Is Back on YouTube, and He Named 2027 for a Tour
posts.excerpt: The hour-long film is back on his YouTube channel after a two-day takedown. After the premiere he said a world tour is coming in 2027, with no cities attached.
posts.body:
Drake put *FOMO* back on YouTube on Thursday, two days after a livestream premiere that he then took down. The film is about an hour long. After the premiere he said a world tour is coming in 2027, with no cities or venues attached.

[youtube:kDK8-psUjzY]

He described the project as self-funded surrealism, a story about making the most of one summer. Cameos include Sexyy Red, Winnie Harlow, and Kevin Durant. Visuals from *Habibti* and *Maid of Honour* sit next to new songs with Don Toliver, Yeat, and PartyNextDoor. In May, *Iceman*, *Habibti*, and *Maid of Honour* made him the first artist to hold the top three slots of the Billboard 200 at once.

"Choosin' Texas," with Don Toliver, remakes Ella Langley's 22-week Hot 100 No. 1. The YouTube version of the film drops Langley from that segment and keeps the song. "Miss My Dawgs," with Yeat, is the first of the unreleased cuts on streaming, on Yeat's *Cocoon* EP. The rest of the hour stays inside the film rather than arriving as a playlist.

The tour talk came in the interview after the premiere, not on a poster. "Obviously, tour is coming and there's other things on the horizon, some big shows," he said. "We'll be out, 2027, to see everybody again across the world." His last North American headline run was *It's All a Blur* in 2023 and 2024. Europe already had *Some Special Shows 4U* with PartyNextDoor in 2025, which he billed as a special. This is the one he is calling a tour, still without a city list.

There is no new Drake album announced inside *FOMO*. The May records are still the last official full-lengths, and most of the new songs are still only in the film. He named 2027 for a tour and did not name a city.

posts.title: ESTRUS
posts.excerpt: A 13-track, 32-minute electro-pop record about wanting everything at once, out today on Pretty Swede and Virgin.
posts.body:
Tove Lo has a habit of naming the mess instead of tidying it. *ESTRUS*, her sixth studio album, is out today on Pretty Swede Records and Virgin Music Group, and the title does the naming first. Estrus, she wrote when the album was announced in May, is an animal in heat, primal, contradicting emotional chaos, a mind and a body that want different things and then want everything. There is no advice on this record. There are thirteen tracks of electro-pop, thirty-two minutes, that refuse to pick a side.

The door was "I'm your girl right?" in May, a pulsing lead single with a Nogari video shot in SГЈo Paulo among seventy dancers. That is the flirtation. "des fleurs," with Stromae, is the album's only collaboration and the one that lets the pulse drop without losing the heat. "DNH" was the bite. "source of life" closed the singles run, a song that runs feral, fragile, numb, and ecstatic in the same breath and then asks the question the rest of the album has been circling. Stay out all night, or stay home and imagine a different life.

[youtube:2SWSD6QVa7c]

The sequencing is short on purpose. It opens with "a lot of feelings, no solutions," fifty seconds of thesis before the first real song. Then the title's weather shows up in "if I could I would," "des fleurs," "DNH," "F.A.M.T." "I'm the cake" is the grin. "the bad one" is the line she has been writing toward for a decade, the one where two things can be true at once. "die for my art with a lonely heart," "are we on a break," "idiot," "roomie." By "source of life" the record has not resolved the argument. It has just named it at every temperature it can reach.

She recorded it with longtime partner Ludvig SГ¶derberg, who still works as A Strut, plus Elvira AnderfjГ¤rd, Luka Kloser, Oscar Holter, OzGo, and TimFromTheHouse, across Los Angeles, Stockholm, and a small fishing village in Sweden where she spent summers as a child. The Knife and Robyn are in the DNA. So is the younger version of herself she went back there to find. *Dirt Femme*, in 2022, was the first record on her own label. Marriage, independence, and four years of unfinished questions sat between that album and this one. *ESTRUS* does not answer them. It puts them on a dance floor and lets them contradict each other in public.

[apple:album:6766440172]

That is the Tove Lo contract, held. *Queen of the Clouds* made the mess famous. *Lady Wood* and *Blue Lips* kept the heat. *Sunshine Kitty* let some light in. *Dirt Femme* was the first time the machinery was hers. *ESTRUS* is the same writer, six albums in, still unwilling to tidy a feeling just because the calendar says she should have grown out of it. She has called the record sexy, twisted, dark, and full of contradictions, and she has said she will keep touring until the obvious joke about age writes itself. That is not a brand refresh. It is a refusal to leave the fight because the fight is the work.

The ESTRUS World Tour is already in motion, which is context, not the point of today. Nashville's Pinnacle and Chicago's Salt Shed opened the North American release run on September 15 and 16. Brooklyn is September 19 at Under The K Bridge, with Cobrah, then Toronto, Los Angeles' Greek Theatre, and Mexico City. Mallrat is on those dates. November takes her through the UK and Europe, the largest headline rooms she has played there, with Rose Gray, through Manchester, Brixton, Brussels, Paris, Amsterdam, Berlin, then Copenhagen, Oslo, and a hometown close at Stockholm's Avicii Arena on November 19. Australia is on the 2027 side of the calendar. None of that has to be chased in order to hear the record.

The tour can wait its turn. Today the argument is thirty-two minutes long, and it does not resolve. That is the point of the title.

posts.title: Pylon
posts.excerpt: Fourteen tracks of diary-entry rock, out today on Dirty Hit and Interscope. The Powerlines Tour, her first arena run, opens October 1.
posts.body:
*Pylon* is out today on Dirty Hit and Interscope, Beatrice Laus's fourth album as beabadoobee and the first one that has to live next to an arena itinerary. It is fourteen tracks of grunge grain, midwest emo, and 1990s radio rock, written on the road while *This Is How Tomorrow Moves* was still behaving like a chart record. That last album was her first UK No. 1. This one is the first time the live map looks like a ledger of rooms that used to be above her.

The title is a piece of infrastructure. Pylons, she has said, were the thing that kept reminding her she was still connected to people while the bus kept moving. The songs started as diary entries she had not said out loud. "A lot of the songs on this record are things I wish I could have said to someone," she said when "Sun Has Set" arrived in June. That single was the first public page, a first-person clip directed by Jake Erland, her partner and longtime visual collaborator, and a vocal with the petty tunnel vision of a letter that never got sent. "It's like, I hate you. You're gonna stay here and listen to how much I hate you. Because I never got to say that."

The sequence does not soften after that. The record opens on the title track, then "Sun Has Set," then "Estranged" and "Switchblade," the second single, which kept the temperature high through July. "Write Me A Letter" sits in the middle of the album with production from Matty Healy and George Daniel of The 1975, Laus's labelmates and longtime collaborators. She has talked about the song as seeing her own fault in a situation and saying the thing she would be too embarrassed to say in the room. "It's Alright," "In Motion," and "Memories" keep the diary moving. "Memories" was the last trailer before release week, and it sounds like the hotel-room version of the writer who used to make demos alone at seventeen.

[youtube:JkB41jZtyrQ]

The guest list is not garnish. "Nothing To Prove" brings Hayley Williams in on a song about taking your power back from fair-weather friends who only want a piece of the success. "Powerlines" carries a verse from Turnstile's Brendan Yates. Chino Moreno of Deftones, Evan Stephens Hall of Pinegrove, and Shane Moran of Title Fight are in the credits too. That is a map of the bands she has been living next to, not a press-kit collage. The people on this record are the ones the isolation kept pointing back toward.

She has said she had to write these songs on tour or between tours because that was the only way to understand what was going on in her head. Letting go. Accepting change. Missing how things were. The hotel rooms reminded her of writing at seventeen, alone in a bedroom, sad as hell, except the rooms outside the window are now arenas. *Pylon* is, in her own framing, an album about accepting that the ugly feelings come back, and that going through them is part of knowing yourself. It is a mid-twenties record that does not pretend the confusion is a phase you graduate from.

[apple:album:6812904778]

The catalog makes the jump visible. *Fake It Flowers* made her a name. *Beatopia* made the name elastic. *This Is How Tomorrow Moves* made the UK chart sit up. *Pylon* is the first time the songs were written in the isolation of a support run and then handed a headline map that can swallow a support run whole. Fourteen tracks. No victory lap. A writer who used the bus as a room.

The Powerlines Tour is the other half of the week, not the substitute for the record. It is her first arena run, promoted by Live Nation, and it opens October 1 at Mohegan Sun Arena in Uncasville, Connecticut, with Wisp. After Uncasville the North American leg runs Philadelphia, Boston, Madison Square Garden on October 5, Toronto, then south and west through the Kia Forum in Los Angeles, wrapping Seattle on October 29. The UK and Europe follow in the autumn, including Glasgow's OVO Hydro, Manchester's AO Arena, and London's O2. Australia is March 2027. This week she is also playing a string of small London release shows, the opposite scale of what October is for. Both are true. Only one of them is the album.

The arenas can wait until October. *Pylon* is already finished. Fourteen songs written in motion, now sitting still long enough to be heard.

posts.title: Olivia Rodrigo's Unraveled Tour Starts Next Week With a Record That Won't Sit Down
posts.excerpt: Hartford is seven days away. *you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love* is still rewriting her own chart records, and the rooms keep getting bigger.
posts.body:
Hartford is seven days away, and the rooms are already too small. Olivia Rodrigo opens the Unraveled Tour on September 25 at PeoplesBank Arena, the first night of a run that began as four Brooklyn dates and then kept multiplying until it looked less like a tour routing and more like a residency map. Ten nights at Los Angeles' Intuit Dome, ten at Barclays Center, eleven at London's O2. Live Nation has the routing. The audience has the receipts. More than a million tickets are already gone.

This is the third album cycle, and it does not behave like a victory lap. *you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love* arrived June 12 on Geffen with a first-week haul of 485,000 equivalent units in the United States, the biggest solo week of 2026, then spent a second week on top of the Billboard 200. In early September it walked back to No. 1 on Top Alternative Albums and Top Rock & Alternative Albums. On the latter list it is now her longest-running leader, past *Guts*. The record is three months old and still arguing with the chart.

[apple:song:6779097512:6779097526]

"drop dead" was the door. It is the song that made the tour announcement sound like a dare instead of a press release. A guitar figure that refuses to sit politely, a vocal that treats heartbreak as a contact sport. The rest of the album is not a sequel to *Sour*'s diary or *Guts*' sneer so much as a third temperature. Rodrigo still writes like someone who cannot leave a feeling half-named. The difference is scale. The feelings got bigger rooms.

Support on select dates comes from Wolf Alice, The Last Dinner Party, Devon Again, Die Spitz, and Grace Ives. That bill is not filler. It is a statement about where she wants the nights to live. Guitar music that can scrape a ceiling, pop that can take a punch, rooms that do not flatten the band into a click track. The outing was drawn for 65 shows. Demand added twenty-five more, including extra London, Amsterdam, Barcelona, and Paris, plus an October 18 date at Boston's TD Garden. The last listed night is May 10, 2027, back at the O2.

[apple:song:6779097512:6779097756]

"the cure" sits further into the album, and it is the one that explains the title. The writing is still sharp enough to bruise, but the arrangement leaves air around the bruise. You can hear why rock radio and the alternative albums chart have not let go. This is not a pop star borrowing a guitar for a costume change. It is a pop star who built the third record so the guitar would have somewhere to live.

Universal Music Canada's June note on the album also listed the hardware around it, limited vinyl, merch drops, collectibles timed to release week. That is the ordinary machinery of a modern campaign. What is less ordinary is the way the live hold keeps tightening after the first-week spike. Most arena tours cool once the album is no longer new. Unraveled is doing the opposite. The album returned to a summit in September. The tour still had not started.

There is a useful comparison inside her own catalog. *Sour* made her a phenomenon. *Guts* made the phenomenon louder and meaner. *you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love* is the first time the phenomenon has to carry a long itinerary and a long chart life at once. A ten-night Intuit Dome stand is a venue record. A double-digit O2 residency puts her in a short list that already includes Prince, the Spice Girls, One Direction, Ariana Grande, Elton John, and Rihanna. Those names are not press-kit garnish. They are a measurement of how many nights a city will buy from one artist before it is full.

The week ahead is logistics. Rehearsals, load-in, the first two Hartford dates on September 25 and 26. After that the map runs through the fall and into a winter of doubled cities, then Europe in the spring. If the album keeps behaving the way it has since June, the set list will not have to chase a fading single. It can play a record that is still moving units while the trucks are on the highway.

That is the story, a week out. The tour is not a victory lap. It is a second argument, made in rooms that keep getting added because the first argument did not finish.

posts.title: Day and Night
posts.excerpt: A 24-song double album, split between live-band daylight pop and after-hours synths, is out today on Schoolboy and Interscope.
posts.body:
Carly Rae Jepsen has a habit of treating time like a writing partner. *Dedicated* had a Side B. *Emotion* had one too. *The Loneliest Time* found a companion in *The Loveliest Time*. *Day and Night*, out today on Schoolboy and Interscope, is the habit made architectural. Twenty-four songs, two discs, one clock. The *Day* disc is twelve tracks of live-band grain and 1970s psychedelic pop. The *Night* disc is twelve more, pulled into synths and the kind of dance music that does not ask permission to stay out. The runtime is just under eighty-five minutes. It does not hurry.

The record was announced on June 22. The first taste was "On Wires," June 26, a daylight song about the impatient early minutes of wanting someone, written with Kyle Shearer and Nate Cyphert. "After All" followed on July 16. "Don't Leave Me on the Dance Floor" arrived August 7. "Motivation" closed the singles run on August 21. Four trailers is a lot for an artist whose cult already knows how to wait. Jepsen used them as weather reports, two for the sun and two for the club.

[apple:album:6781767022]

The official framing is a twenty-four-hour blur. Nights stretch into mornings. Days dissolve into nights. You are supposed to feel suspended inside a single long hour. That is marketing language, and it happens to describe the sequencing. "After All" opens the *Day* disc like a window being lifted. "Habits of Creatures" and "Versailles" keep the light in the room. "On Wires," track four, is the impatient heart of the disc. Shearer's production, a vocal that leans forward as if the chorus might leave without her. By "Just a Little Walk on the Moon," the daylight side has walked itself out to the edge of evening.

*Night* starts with "Never Let a Good Thing Die," the longest cut on the album, and then the temperature changes. "Amalfi Coast," "Patience Power Passion," "Don't Leave Me on the Dance Floor," "Motivation." The second disc is not a remix of the first. It is the same writer staying up. Collaborators include Tavish Crowe, Shearer, Cyphert, and Cole M.G.N., Jepsen's husband, alongside Noonie Bao, Patrik Berger, Markus Krunegard, and Pontus Winnberg. The credits read like a map of the last decade of smart pop, from Stockholm and Los Angeles, the *Emotion* brain trust, the people who know how to make a chorus feel expensive without making it cheap.

Critics got the album a few days early, and the early scores have been generally favorable, with Metacritic sitting near 80. *The Line of Best Fit* called it her most far-reaching work. *Rolling Stone* heard a dissertation on love, which is a grand way of saying Jepsen is still writing about the same subject she has always written about, only with more rooms in the house. *Paste* liked the textures. *Slant Magazine*, less convinced, found it sonically adventurous and a little unwieldy, which is a fair warning about a double album. *NME* said it grows. *The Times* wondered if the length was a mistake. None of that is a consensus. It is a split that a twenty-four-track pop record should expect.

What is not in dispute is the shape. Jepsen has spent a decade proving that pop can be meticulous without being cold. *Emotion*'s tenth anniversary show at the Troubadour last August was a reminder of that contract. Play the album in order, take the choruses seriously, do not wink so hard the songs collapse. *Day and Night* is the first new full-length since that night, and it sounds like someone who heard the crowd sing the old precision and decided the new precision could be longer.

She launches the album onstage September 27, headlining New York's All Things Go Festival, her first billed performance of 2026, on a bill that also includes Zara Larsson, Lola Young, Brandi Carlile, and MUNA. A festival slot is a strange place to debut a double album. It is also the right kind of strange. You cannot play twenty-four songs. You can play the argument. A song from the *Day* disc, a song from *Night*, proof that the two halves talk to each other.

The Japanese CD tacks on "Reaching for a Star" and "Yes." That is a regional extra, not a third disc. The album as written is twenty-four songs and two clocks. *Day and Night* is for people who will sit with both hours, not for the loudest person in the room.
